headline: Mind Robotics, the robot start-up led by Rivian's chief executive, has hired former Ford and Apple executive Doug Field as its president.
score_reason: Pool score 5 kept: a senior hire at a well-funded robotics start-up that has shown no robot yet.
importance_line: Engineers and workers in Rivian's factories are the first likely users, and the hire shows senior car-industry talent moving into physical AI, but no robot has been shown and the company has not said what form its robots will take.
summary: The Verge reports that Mind Robotics, a robotics start-up founded in 2025 by RJ Scaringe, Rivian's chief executive and Mind's acting chief executive, has appointed Doug Field, Ford's former electric vehicle and software chief and a former Tesla and Apple engineering executive, as president to run its effort to build what it calls universally capable robots for Rivian's factories and other uses. Mind Robotics, which is a partner of Rivian rather than a spin-off, is partly owned by Rivian, which will be its first customer, and has raised more than $1 billion without yet showing a robot in public.
notes: Read in full from the pool fulltext. The Verge corrected the story on 13 Oct 2026: Mind Robotics is a partner of Rivian, not a spin-off; the wording follows the correction.
